summary: Follow-up of the accepted U.1 packet. Refine only its unfinished relative K1 comparison: the square of plus maps gives a concrete congruence-loop map, whose kernel is determined by the Steinberg reduction map. Identify the degree-two connecting map with an inverse lifted word under the pinned fibre convention, and import the already-owned degree-zero patching comparison. Preserve the parent congruence groups, transfers, norms, projection formula and DVR boundary by reference. This is a complete planning pass with precise supplier requests, not a claim of implementation or gap-free closure.

nodes.title: Steinberg group of the acyclic plus fibre
nodes.statement: Write G_R=GL(R), P_R=E(R), j_R:BG_R→BG_R⁺ and V_R=fib(j_R) with paths j_R(x)→base. There is a unique isomorphism κ_R:π1(V_R)≃St(R) over P_R, hence over G_R. Its restriction to the kernel identifies ∂j_R:π2(BG_R⁺)→π1(V_R) with the inclusion of classical K2(R)=ker φ_R in St(R). Define β_R:K2(R)≃π2(BG_R⁺) as the inverse of that restricted map; this fixes its sign.
hypotheses: A is an associative unital ring, I is a two-sided ideal, B=A/I, and q:A→B is the quotient map.
All linear, elementary and Steinberg groups are stable groups; no finite-rank assertion is inferred.
proofSteps: H.3 identifies π1(V_R)→P_R as a universal central extension. T.1 supplies St(R)→P_R as another; uniqueness and rigidity give the unique isomorphism over P_R.
The fibre long exact sequence and π2(BG_R)=0 make ∂j_R injective with image ker(π1(V_R)→G_R). Transport that kernel through κ_R to ker φ_R.
Invert this particular map to obtain β_R. Do not silently replace it by an uncalibrated Hurewicz isomorphism.
acceptance: All maps preserve the displayed basepoint and the specified loop orientation.

nodes.title: Naturality of the whole Steinberg identification
nodes.statement: For a unital ring map f:R→S and a based functorial square of plus maps, κ_S∘π1(V_f)=St(f)∘κ_R. Consequently β_S∘K2(f)=π2(BGL(f)⁺)∘β_R.
hypotheses: A is an associative unital ring, I is a two-sided ideal, B=A/I, and q:A→B is the quotient map.
All linear, elementary and Steinberg groups are stable groups; no finite-rank assertion is inferred.
proofSteps: Both candidate maps between the two central extensions lift E(f). Pull back the target extension along E(f); uniqueness of the lift from the source UCE identifies them.
Check that St(f) lifts E(f) on root generators. This proves naturality of the full group, not merely its central kernel.
Naturality of the fibre boundary then gives the displayed β square. Based coherent squares are part of the supplier interface; arbitrary independently chosen free homotopies are not used.

nodes.title: Image of the Steinberg reduction kernel
nodes.statement: For q:A→A/I, φ_A(ker St(q))=E(A,I) as subgroups of GL(A). This is the normal closure inside E(A), not inside GL(A), before stable normality is invoked.
hypotheses: A is an associative unital ring, I is a two-sided ideal, B=A/I, and q:A→B is the quotient map.
All linear, elementary and Steinberg groups are stable groups; no finite-rank assertion is inferred.
proofSteps: Use request R-St-quotient: St(q) is onto and its kernel is the normal closure in St(A) of all x_ij(x), x∈I.
The Steinberg map onto E(A) sends precisely those generators to e_ij(x). Apply the pinned normal-closure image theorem to this surjection with codomain E(A), then embed into GL(A).
This identifies both images by their conjugate generators. The fact that GL(A)→GL(A/I) can fail to be onto is irrelevant.
acceptance: I=0 gives the trivial image.
For I=A and B the zero ring, the image is E(A).
Conjugators are lifted through St(A)→E(A); no finite-rank normality assumption is inserted.

nodes.title: The component of the unmodified reduction fibre
nodes.statement: Let F0=fib(BGL(q)). The map BGL(A,I)→F0 given by the inclusion of N=ker GL(q) and its constant reduction null-homotopy is a based weak equivalence onto the basepoint path component of F0. It induces π1(F0)≃N, with projection to GL(A) the subgroup inclusion. This assertion needs no surjectivity of GL(q).
hypotheses: A is an associative unital ring, I is a two-sided ideal, B=A/I, and q:A→B is the quotient map.
All linear, elementary and Steinberg groups are stable groups; no finite-rank assertion is inferred.
proofSteps: Classifying spaces are K(G,1). Their fibre sequence gives πn(F0)=0 for n≥2 and identifies π1(F0) with ker GL(q).
The constant null-homotopy of the composite BN→BG_A→BG_B gives the actual comparison. Its π1 map is the kernel inclusion by naturality of the group/classifying-space identification.
The domain is connected, so its image lies in the basepoint component, and the map is a weak equivalence there. Other components are controlled by the image cosets of GL(q), not assumed absent.
acceptance: Reduction GL(Z)→GL(F5) is not onto: determinant ±1 cannot reach determinant 2. The identity-component statement still applies.

nodes.title: Congruence matrices as relative plus loops
nodes.statement: Define c_I:N=GL(A,I)→π1(F⁺), F⁺=fib(BGL(q)⁺), by the map BN→F0→F⁺ induced by the based square of plus maps and its specified homotopy. A matrix loop with constant reduction is sent to its plus loop together with the resulting reduction path. The square homotopy H has direction j_B∘BGL(q)→BGL(q)⁺∘j_A. The induced F0→F⁺ map uses its reversal; it is part of the map even when one strictifies the square.
hypotheses: A is an associative unital ring, I is a two-sided ideal, B=A/I, and q:A→B is the quotient map.
All linear, elementary and Steinberg groups are stable groups; no finite-rank assertion is inferred.
proofSteps: Use the constant null-homotopy to construct BN→F0.

Apply the based-square fibre map for the chosen plus square. In a homotopy-commuting model, concatenate its square homotopy with the image of the old fibre path, with the orientation required by paths f(x)→base.
Apply π1 and the classifying-space comparison to obtain the group homomorphism. Functoriality is through coherent based squares, so no free-homotopy basepoint-change action is used.

nodes.title: A fibre sequence from the square of plus maps
nodes.statement: Put V_A=fib(j_A), V_B=fib(j_B), and W=fib(V_A→V_B). The based plus square induces a fibre sequence W→F0→F⁺. Under π1(F0)≃N and κ_A:π1(V_A)≃St(A), the composite π1(W)→π1(F0)→GL(A) equals φ_A composed with π1(W)→π1(V_A)→St(A).

proofSteps: Invoke request R-fibre-interchange for this based square. It identifies the two iterated homotopy fibres, compatibly with projections, without declaring the original square homotopy-cartesian.
In the path-square model, the two descriptions specify a point and two paths with a filling homotopy. Swap the two path directions; prefix contractions give the inverse equivalence.
Compatibility of both projections gives the displayed identity on π1. This identifies the kernel image in the subsequent argument rather than comparing unnamed exact sequences.

sourceIssues.locator: III.5.3 central-extension classification paragraph, printed p.218 / PDF226, contrasted with III.5.3.1 discussion on printed p.219 / PDF227, combined author manuscript dated 29 August 2013.
sourceIssues.printed: The classification of central extensions with arbitrary abelian kernel A is written with integral cohomology H²(G;Z).
sourceIssues.correction: Use H²(G;A), with trivial G-action on A. Integral coefficients describe the case A=Z. The following page itself uses A as the coefficient group.
sourceIssues.reason: A central-extension cocycle takes values in its kernel A. For G=C2 and A=0 there is only the identity extension, whereas H²(C2;Z)=Z/2; integral coefficients cannot classify that kernel. The next-page argument uses A. The proof here uses UCE uniqueness and never the erroneous coefficient.
sourceIssues.known: The next-page discussion in the same author copy uses H²(G;A), making the intended coefficient clear; no separate published correction was verified.
